why: All three checks confirm the finding. (1) The quote is verbatim: whats-new/index.md line 54 reads in full 'Also this week: **sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents** (background chains are capped at five levels deep); **`--safe-mode`** starts Claude Code with all customizations disabled for troubleshooting; and **`fallbackModel`** configures up to three fallback models tried in order.' Nothing in the line reverses it; the Week-24 digest (whats-new/2026-w24.md:69) and model-config.md:361-367 corroborate: 'Configure one or more fallback models and Claude Code tries them in order... Chains are capped at three models after duplicate removal, and extra entries are ignored', with `--fallback-model` accepting a comma-separated list and the settings key accepting an array. (2) Our state is as claimed, with a ~5-line citation drift: packages/shared/src/config/config-defaults-schema.ts:51-52 is exact ('Pi model ID to retry once after model/network drain errors. Empty disables fallback.' / `fallbackModel: string;`); packages/shared/src/config/validators.ts:135 is `fallbackModel: z.string()`; the default lives at storage.ts:194 (cited as :189) as `fallbackModel: ''`; the non-string coercion lives at storage.ts:273-276 (cited as :268-271) as `typeof ... === 'string' ? ....trim() : ''`, reinforced by `normalizePiFallbackModelId` (config/models-pi.ts:20-22, same string-or-empty coercion). No `fallbackModels` array, no comma-splitting, no dedupe, no three-entry cap, no 'default' keyword expansion anywhere in the repo (checked with grep -a, so NUL-byte files are covered). (3) The consequence is verified separately from the identifier and holds: pi-agent.ts:6313-6324 `getRetryFallbackModel` returns at most that one id and returns null when `options.fallbackModelRetry` is already set; :6326-6344 `retryWithFallbackModel` setModel()s to it and re-enters chatImpl with `fallbackModelRetry: true`, so a second drain error has nowhere to go — exactly one hop, not a chain. It is reached from the two live error paths at :6755-6757 and :6795-6797, so the setting is wired, not inert. Not an owner decision: 'fallback' does not appear anywhere in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md, and none of the nine dated decisions in section 3 touches it. Not a de-brand or dropped-subscription product difference either — this is a Pi-runtime retry knob our fork implements itself, on its primary runtime. Sibling-subsystem check: the key is Pi-only; packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts never sets `fallbackModel`, so naming Pi is correct and the Claude backend has no fallback at all. f242 duplicates f226 (whats-new/2026-w24) and overlaps f106 (model-config) and f113 (admin-setup) — same underlying single-string arity, restated by the digest index; duplication corroborates rather than refutes. Note for the register: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:110 (from plans/2026-07-29-effort-precedence.md:199) says the string is 'read by nothing' — that half is stale, pi-agent.ts:6257 reads it.
correctedState: `fallbackModel` is a single string in our fork, not an ordered chain: `fallbackModel: z.string()` (packages/shared/src/config/validators.ts:135), default `''` (packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:194), and any non-string value is coerced to `''` on load (storage.ts:273-276, plus `normalizePiFallbackModelId` in config/models-pi.ts:20-22) — so a settings file written in Claude's array form configures nothing. At runtime it is Pi-only and does exactly one hop: `getRetryFallbackModel` (pi-agent.ts:6313-6324) yields that single id for the drain/overload error codes in `FALLBACK_MODEL_RETRY_ERROR_CODES` and returns null once `fallbackModelRetry` is set, and `retryWithFallbackModel` (:6326-6344) retries once with that flag, so a second failure has no further target. There is no comma-separated `--fallback-model` parsing, no duplicate removal, no three-entry cap and no `"default"` keyword. Two further divergences the finding did not state: the switch is not turn-scoped — `this.setModel(fallbackModel)` (:6335) leaves the session on the fallback model, where Claude documents the switch as lasting the current turn only — and the Claude backend (packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts) never passes `fallbackModel` to the SDK at all, so on that backend there is no fallback whatsoever. The key is also file-editable only; no UI writes it.
